key_insight: MIRROR exploits the fact that text, image, and combined views of the same geometry problem reveal complementary reasoning strengths and failures, using the best view to teach the others.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical training recipe for making vision-language models more reliable and consistent across modalities in multimodal reasoning systems.
method: Build ODA-Data: paired geometry problems with text-dominant, image-dominant, and combined views.
Evaluate the model on all views for each problem and choose the best-performing view as the teacher.
Apply a reverse-KL reinforcement learning objective to align weaker views toward the teacher view.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over standard RL across geometry reasoning benchmarks, with better accuracy and more consistent behavior across modalities.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality paired multimodal data and view-wise evaluation, so gains may be sensitive to dataset construction and teacher-view selection.
paper_title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
